alternative: A typed worker pool (Node worker_threads or Web Workers, messages validated at the boundary) for CPU-bound work; async/await with Promise.all for I/O-bound fan-out.
idiom_name: none in-language; a typed Worker pool is the substitute
implementation_notes: TypeScript compiles to JavaScript, so the execution model is the same single-threaded event loop: types improve the worker protocol (message unions, typed facades) but add neither parallelism nor a pool. CPU-bound fork/join still needs Worker threads, with the join expressed as promises over postMessage/'message' events; the compiler cannot type-check values crossing the structured-clone boundary, so validate them at the worker edge or rely on a pool library that does. For I/O-bound fan-out, async/await plus Promise.all (typed with Awaited) remains the idiomatic substitute for a fork/join that the platform cannot provide in-process.
pitfalls: Structured clone ignores the type system: interfaces crossing postMessage arrive as plain objects - classes, methods and prototypes do not survive.
Promise.all over async tasks is concurrency, not parallelism: CPU-bound code still runs on one thread, so it cannot replace fork/join for compute.
The worker boundary is an unchecked any unless messages are validated at runtime (type predicates/schema), and a typed facade hides that hole.
